issues.quote:
Take your time. What did you hear after that?

FÉLIX: At a quarter past ten by my watch someone went quickly up the stairs past the library door.
issues.fact: F4 gives the stairs event at a quarter past ten, which is earlier than the eighteen-minutes-past-ten thump and repeater in F3. The sheet does not say the stairs event came after the repeater.
issues.misreading: The question 'What did you hear after that?' asks for events following the thump and repeater, so a solver could read the 10:15 up-the-stairs movement as happening after 10:18. That reverses the order the clock readings give and changes the sequence a solver would build.

issues.quote: and it has never kept proper time since the day he gave it to me.
issues.fact: The sheet gives only the readings 'by my watch' and says the watch showed twenty minutes to nine when the bell struck nine. It does not say the watch is inaccurate or by how much.
issues.misreading: Saying the watch 'never kept proper time' invites a solver to treat every watch reading as wrong and to correct them by an offset, most likely the twenty minutes implied at dinner. That changes what each stated reading means in true time, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: A debtor under the room where the old man lay down?
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the thump was on the floor above the library, in the atelier. It does not say where the uncle was, or that he lay down there, at any time.
issues.misreading: The phrase 'the room where the old man lay down' suggests the uncle was in the atelier, possibly lying down, when the thump and repeater sounded. That is a whereabouts the sheet does not give.
